### Position read
Opening position. Red has moved from (0,3) to the center at (3,3); losses are 0–0 for every color. The piece is not immediately sandwichable because no opponent has a same-color far flank on its row or column.

### Our plan
Contest the center early with supported Red and Yellow pieces. On Yellow’s turn, reassess all four central squares and occupy one if safe, preferably creating a diagonal or adjacent pair without exposing a multi-capture. Build same-color flank geometry before attempting sandwiches.

### Opponent tendencies
Unknown. Watch whether Blue immediately contests row 3 or another central square, and whether Green mirrors from the left.

### Lessons
Captures only trigger from the mover’s landing square. Moving into apparent sandwich geometry is safe, but every piece left behind must be checked against opponent landing squares and same-color far flanks.

### Position read
We hold center squares (3,3) with Red and (4,3) with Yellow. Blue occupies (3,4). Losses remain 0–0. Blue cannot move again before Red, and Green cannot obstruct the clear Red route from (0,5) to (3,5).

### Our plan
On Red’s next turn, play (0,5)->(3,5), sandwiching and capturing Blue at (3,4) against Red at (3,3), unless the board changes unexpectedly. If Blue then enters (4,4) from (4,7), Yellow can answer (7,5)->(4,5), capturing it against Yellow at (4,3). Continue converting these same-color flank pairs into center control.

### Opponent tendencies
Blue contested the center immediately with (3,7)->(3,4), but entered a forced Red sandwich because its turn does not recur before Red’s.

### Lessons
Exploit turn order when an opponent center piece cannot escape before our matching-color flank closes. Adjacent teammate pieces support center occupation but never serve as sandwich partners.

### Position read
Red’s move to (3,5) captures Blue at (3,4) against Red at (3,3), giving Blue 1 loss. We hold center squares (3,3) with Red and (4,3) with Yellow; (3,4) and (4,4) are empty. Green is staged at (5,4).

### Our plan
If Blue enters (4,4) from the right, answer on Yellow’s turn with (7,5)->(4,5), sandwiching it against Yellow at (4,3). Otherwise seek a safe Yellow occupation of (4,4) or reinforce the center while checking Green’s potential entry from (5,4). Build same-color flanks around any opponent center intruder.

### Opponent tendencies
Blue contests the center directly even when turn order permits an immediate sandwich. Green has moved inward to (5,4), likely preparing to enter or pressure the center.

### Lessons
Turn-order traps are decisive: an opponent piece placed between an existing same-color anchor and a reachable landing square can be removed before it escapes. Recheck Green’s nearby geometry before every center occupation.

### Position read
We hold center squares (3,3) with Red and (4,4) with Yellow. Blue has 1 loss and remains at (4,5), directly beside the Yellow anchor. Green is staged at (5,4). All our colors remain lossless.

### Our plan
If Blue remains at (4,5) through its turn, play Yellow (7,6)->(4,6) to sandwich it against Yellow at (4,4), raising Blue to 2 losses. If Green enters (4,3), Yellow (7,2)->(4,2) sandwiches it against (4,4). Use Red’s next turn to secure (3,4) if safe or build pressure while retaining Red at (3,3).

### Opponent tendencies
Blue contests central lanes despite same-color sandwich anchors. Green is poised beside the center and may seek (4,3), but that square is now tactically trapped by Yellow.

### Lessons
A center occupation is strongest when it also becomes a stationary sandwich flank. Check whether the opponent can block the planned landing square or remove the anchor before the capturing color acts.

### Position read
We hold three center squares: Red at (3,3),(3,4) and Yellow at (4,4). Green occupies the last center (4,3). Blue has 1 loss and is exposed at (4,5). We remain lossless.

### Our plan
Yellow has a fork: (7,2)->(4,2) sandwiches Green at (4,3) against Yellow (4,4), while (7,6)->(4,6) sandwiches Blue at (4,5) against the same anchor. After Blue moves, capture whichever target remains. If Green is removed, aim to occupy (4,3) for an immediate center win; protect the Yellow anchor at (4,4).

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent contests center despite same-color sandwich geometry. Blue may flee (4,5) or block Yellow’s c2 route from (6,7) to (6,2), but cannot neutralize both capture threats in one move.

### Lessons
Central anchors can generate threats on both sides. Recheck that (4,4) remains occupied and the selected Yellow landing lane is clear before executing the capture.

### Position read
We hold Red at (3,3),(3,4) and Yellow at (4,4), while Green holds the last center (4,3). Blue blocked the c2 Yellow lane with (6,2), so Yellow captured Blue at (4,5) by landing (4,6). Blue now has 2 losses; we remain lossless.

### Our plan
Blue is one capture from elimination. Preserve Yellow (4,4), which supports center control and same-color sandwiches. If Green vacates (4,3), occupy it for an immediate center win. Otherwise reopen or create a Yellow landing at (4,2) to sandwich Green against (4,4), while seeking any safe Blue capture.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent uses blocking moves to break one arm of a fork, but the other arm remained actionable. Expect Green to disrupt the central Yellow anchor or reinforce (4,3), and Blue to prioritize survival at two losses.

### Lessons
After a blocking reply, verify both fork lanes independently and execute the intact capture. A color at two losses becomes the primary tactical target, but an immediate center completion remains higher priority.

### Position read
We have Red at (3,3) and newly staged at (5,2); Green occupies (4,3), with Green support at (5,4) and (2,4). Blue has 2 losses, while Red and Yellow each have 1 after Green’s mixed double capture.

### Our plan
Threaten Red (5,2)->(5,3), sandwiching Green (4,3) against Red (3,3). If Green blocks by occupying (5,3) or vacates the center, exploit the resulting displacement. Yellow (4,6) can enter (4,4) to rebuild center presence. Continue prioritizing any safe capture of Blue, which is one loss from elimination.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent actively identifies mixed-color sandwich lines and uses blocking moves to disrupt threats. Expect Blue to aid Green’s defense where possible and Green (5,4) to consider blocking (5,3).

### Lessons
Green’s last move showed that aligned teammate pieces are equally vulnerable inside an opponent-colored sandwich. Preserve the Red anchor at (3,3) while using a second Red to attack the center with a valid same-color flank.

### Position read
Red anchors (3,3) with its attacker at (5,2); Green at (4,3) is threatened by Red (5,2)->(5,3). Yellow now stages at (3,5) while retaining Yellow (4,6). Blue remains one loss from elimination.

### Our plan
If Green blocks the Red sandwich by moving (5,4)->(5,3), contest (4,4) with Yellow from (4,6); vacating (5,4) removes Green’s immediate vertical sandwich geometry there. If Green instead evacuates (4,3), use the released center space. Keep the staged Yellow at (3,5) as a second route toward (3,4) or lateral support. Take any safe Blue capture immediately.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent sees mixed-color sandwich tactics and favors direct blocking. Expect Green to defend (4,3), most naturally with (5,4)->(5,3), while Blue may reposition near the staged Yellow.

### Lessons
Center entries must be checked against same-color far flanks. Preserve multiple approach squares so one defensive move cannot shut down both colors’ central pressure.

### Position read
Red now anchors (3,3) and (5,3), having captured Green at (4,3). Green still occupies (4,4), while (3,4) and (4,3) are open. Yellow is staged at (3,5) and (4,6). Blue remains at two losses, one capture from elimination.

### Our plan
On Yellow’s turn, strongly consider (3,5)->(3,4) if Blue does not create an urgent threat; entering between Green (2,4) and (4,4) is safe because captures trigger only on the mover’s landing. Then develop same-color flanks to remove Green from (4,4) and occupy the lower center. Take any safe Blue capture immediately.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent uses direct central blocks and may reposition Blue against the staged Yellow. Green’s remaining center pair at (2,4) and (4,4) creates future sandwich geometry but cannot capture a piece merely entering (3,4).

### Lessons
Exploit triggered sandwiches immediately when they remove center defenders. A piece may safely enter an existing enemy sandwich, but future enemy flank moves and enclosure threats still require checking.

### Position read
We hold (3,3) with Red and now (3,4) with Yellow; Green holds (4,4), while (4,3) is open. Yellow at (3,4) sits between Green at (2,4) and (4,4) but is safe because no Green move created that sandwich. Blue has two losses and pieces at (1,7), (3,7), (5,4), and (6,2). Blue threatens to sandwich Red (5,3) by moving (6,2)->(5,2) while (5,4) remains the far flank.

### Our plan
On Red’s next turn, answer the Blue threat at row 5 unless Green creates something more urgent: move Red (5,3) safely or disrupt the Blue flank. Preserve our two occupied upper-center squares. Build Yellow geometry around Green (4,4), ideally placing a Yellow at (4,5) and later landing another at (4,3) to capture it. Any safe capture of Blue immediately eliminates Blue.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent contests the center directly and builds same-color sandwich flanks. Expect Green to vacate or reposition one of the vertical flanks around Yellow (3,4), possibly intending to return later and trigger the capture.

### Lessons
Existing enemy flanks do not capture a piece that moves between them. Recheck whether either flank can vacate and return before the exposed piece’s next turn. Protect colors from double captures and prioritize Blue’s third loss.

### Position read
We occupy (3,3), (3,4), and (4,3); Green occupies the final center (4,4). Red’s move from (5,3) escaped Blue’s threatened (6,2)->(5,2) sandwich. Blue remains one capture from elimination. Green deliberately moved (2,4)->(2,3), creating the threat (2,3)->(2,4) next Green turn, which would sandwich Yellow (3,4) against Green (4,4).

### Our plan
On Yellow’s next turn, unless Blue creates a winning emergency, move Yellow (3,4) out of Green’s vertical sandwich before Green acts. Preserve Red at (3,3) and (4,3), contest (4,4), and seek any safe Blue capture for immediate elimination. After Yellow evacuates, rebuild support for the center without exposing two pieces to one sandwich.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent uses vacate-and-return sandwich triggers and contests the center directly. Expect Blue to improve its center access or reposition its vulnerable piece at (6,2); expect Green to return to (2,4) if Yellow remains on (3,4).

### Lessons
A flank that vacates can return to trigger a previously harmless sandwich. Track such one-turn threats through the full turn order. Same-color flanks remain essential; teammate pieces do not complete captures.

### Position read
We hold center squares (3,3) and (4,3); Green holds (4,4). Yellow escaped from (3,4) to (2,4), neutralizing Green’s threatened return to (2,4). Blue remains one loss from elimination, with pieces at (1,7), (3,7), (5,3), and (6,2).

### Our plan
Preserve the two Red center pieces and hunt any safe Blue capture for immediate elimination. Yellow at (2,4) and Yellow at (4,6) create a tactical idea: if Green vacates (4,4) for (3,4), Yellow can potentially play (4,6)->(4,4), sandwiching Green vertically against Yellow (2,4). Continue building same-color flank geometry and avoid exposing multiple pieces in one line.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent uses vacate-and-return sandwiches and direct center occupation. Expect Green to avoid stepping onto (3,4) if the Yellow vertical trap remains available; Blue may reposition its vulnerable pieces or challenge Red’s center structure.

### Lessons
Evacuating a threatened piece can also create a counter-capture flank. Recheck whether a center move by the opponent opens its former square as the landing point needed to complete a sandwich.

### Position read
We hold center squares (3,3) and (4,3); Green holds (4,4), while (3,4) is empty. Blue remains one loss from elimination at (1,7), (3,7), (5,3), and (6,2). Red advanced to (3,6), pinning Blue’s (3,7) against the edge and creating a route to (3,4). Yellow at (2,4) is threatened by Green’s (1,5) landing on (2,5).

### Our plan
On Yellow’s turn, first ensure (2,4) is not freely captured; consider whether a tactical counter or evacuation is best. Red aims to play (3,6)->(3,4), giving us three center squares while keeping (3,3) and (4,3). Pressure Green at (4,4), and seize it with Yellow from (4,6) if it vacates. Continue hunting one safe Blue capture for elimination.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent uses vacate-and-return sandwiches and direct center occupation. Green may play (1,5)->(2,5) to capture Yellow at (2,4), while Blue may try to free its edge piece or reposition vulnerable pieces.

### Lessons
Edge pieces can be constrained by occupying their only inward lane. Preserve established center holders while bringing a separate piece into the remaining center square.

### Position read
We hold center squares (3,3) and (4,3); Green holds (4,4), and (3,4) is empty. Yellow’s move (7,2)->(2,2) sandwiches Green at (2,3) against Yellow (2,4), raising Green to 2 losses while preserving the threatened Yellow. Blue is also at 2 losses, with pieces at (1,2), (1,7), (3,7), and (5,3).

### Our plan
Both opponent colors are now one capture from elimination. Red should seek a safe Blue capture, especially the constrained edge Blue at (3,7), while retaining our two center holders. Red’s route (3,6)->(3,4) can claim a third center square if tactically safe. Yellow should pressure Green (4,4) and exploit any same-color flank formed by Yellow (2,2) and (2,4).

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent uses vacate-and-return sandwiches and direct center occupation. Green must now protect every normal piece because one more Green loss eliminates the color; Blue faces the same constraint.

### Lessons
Look for long rook advances that complete an existing same-color sandwich. A capture can simultaneously remove a threat and push a color to the brink of elimination.

### Position read
We occupy three center squares: Red at (3,3), (3,4), and (4,3). Green occupies the last center square at (4,4). Both opponent colors remain at 2 losses, so either is eliminated by one further capture. Blue pieces are at (1,2), (1,7), (3,7), and (5,3); Green pieces are at (1,3), (3,0), (4,4), and (6,0).

### Our plan
Remove Green from (4,4), then occupy that square for an immediate center win. Red’s same-color anchor at (4,3) can sandwich Green if a Red piece can land at (4,5). Preserve all three center holders and watch Blue (5,3), which lies beside Red (4,3). Yellow should maintain the (2,2)/(2,4) pair and seek the final Green capture.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent uses vacate-and-return sandwiches and direct center occupation. With both colors at 2 losses, they must avoid every capture while urgently disrupting our three-square center majority.

### Lessons
Same-color geometry is decisive: teammate pieces cannot complete sandwiches. Before moving a center holder, check whether the move sacrifices the center threat or exposes a multi-capture.

### Position read
We hold Red at three center squares: (3,3), (3,4), and (4,3). Green at (4,4) is the only obstacle. Yellow now occupies (4,5), leaving Green’s center piece with only downward mobility. Both opponent colors have 2 losses, so one capture eliminates either color.

### Our plan
If Green remains at (4,4), preserve the Red center wall and play Yellow (7,4)->(5,4) when possible to complete an enclosure and eliminate Green. If Green vacates (4,4), aim to move Yellow from (4,5) into it for an immediate center win. On the intervening Red turn, defend all three center holders and avoid vacating one unless forced.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent uses direct center occupation and vacate-and-return sandwich ideas. Green must now escape downward, break a center holder, or prevent Yellow’s enclosure; Blue’s likely task is disrupting the Red center before Yellow can enter (4,4).

### Lessons
A near-complete enclosure can force a center occupant to flee. Preserve the three existing center squares while the outside Yellow piece supplies the fourth.

### Position read
Red (3,3) moved to (3,1), breaking Blue’s dangerous (1,2)->(1,3) sandwich through Green (2,3) and both central Reds. We retain Red at (3,4) and (4,3), while Green (4,4) remains caught in Yellow’s column-four geometry. Both opponent colors still have 2 losses.

### Our plan
After Blue moves, play Yellow along column 4: normally (7,4)->(5,4), sandwiching Green (4,4) and Red (3,4) against Yellow (2,4), eliminating Green. If Blue interposes at (5,4), use (7,4)->(6,4) to capture the entire intervening line and potentially eliminate both opponent colors. Keep Red (4,3) blocking Blue’s center entry.

### Opponent tendencies
Blue’s strongest hidden resource was the long sandwich from (1,3) to its piece at (5,3); that line is now broken by the empty (3,3). Expect Blue to disrupt the Yellow anchor at (2,4), vacate (5,3), or seek another center intrusion.

### Lessons
Scan long mixed-color lines before committing to center tactics. A single evacuation can prevent a double capture while preserving the decisive same-color flank elsewhere.

### Position read
Yellow’s move from (7,4) to (6,4) creates a same-color sandwich against Yellow at (2,4), capturing Blue (5,4), Green (4,4), and Red (3,4).

### Our plan
The capture raises both opponent colors from 2 losses to 3, eliminating both immediately and winning the game by team elimination. Our Red incurs friendly fire but remains below elimination.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent interposed Blue at (5,4), but this extended rather than disrupted the mixed-color capture line.

### Lessons
A sandwich may capture a mixed line of enemy and teammate pieces. When both opponent colors are at 2 losses, one such move can eliminate the entire opposing team despite acceptable friendly fire.
